name: Zermatt Village Center
description: The lively core of the resort, running along the pedestrian Bahnhofstrasse from the train station to the old church. Here you find the hotels, restaurants, shops, apres-ski bars and the buzz of arriving visitors, all within an easy flat walk of everything.
bestFor: First-timers who want to be walking distance from everything
pros: Best choice of dining and shops
Direct access to the train and lifts
cons: Can feel crowded in peak season

name: Winkelmatten
tagline: A quieter residential quarter with Matterhorn views
description: A calmer village quarter just south of the center, set slightly uphill with its own small chapel and lovely open outlooks toward the Matterhorn. It is residential and peaceful, popular with those wanting a quieter base still connected to town by a short walk or the e-bus.
bestFor: Slow travelers wanting quiet and views near the center
pros: Short walk or e-bus to the center

name: Zmutt
tagline: A tiny historic hamlet above the valley
description: A cluster of old timber chalets and barns up the valley west of Zermatt, reached on foot along a scenic trail. Famous for its rustic mountain restaurants, it is not a place to base yourself but a beloved day-hike destination for an authentic Valais meal with a view.
bestFor: Day hikers seeking old-world charm and mountain dining

name: Tasch
tagline: The car park and rail gateway to Zermatt
description: The last point cars can reach before Zermatt, a few minutes down the valley. Visitors park in its large garages and hop on the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn shuttle up to the resort. Quieter and cheaper than Zermatt, it works as a budget-conscious base with an easy train link.
pros: Quick train shuttle into the resort
cons: You must train in for the mountains
